qAndA.question: How does the instructor demonstrate a lunar eclipse in the model?

activities.description: Instructor introduces the topic of eclipses and demonstrates using a model with discs, balls, and a snake light.
Explains the scale of the model and the exaggerated tilt of the moon's orbit.
Emphasizes the actual tilt of the moon's orbit compared to Earth's orbit.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The scene sets the stage for exploring why eclipses don't occur every month.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduces the concept of eclipses and explains the model's limitations.

activities.description: Instructor asks why eclipses don't happen every month.
Explains the tilt of the moon's orbit and distributes models to students.
Students position their models to represent the Earth-Moon-Sun system.
Instructor checks for lunar eclipses in each model.
Students move their models to represent the full moon position and check again for lunar eclipses.
Instructor suggests moving the moon to the new moon position to explore solar eclipses.
